claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an FCC matrix.
The as-built alloy possesses a native thin oxide scale originating from processing.
The native oxide scale is protective under the relevant elevated-temperature exposure conditions.
Exposure to a reducing gas destabilizes or partially reduces the protective oxide layer.
Oxide destabilization under reducing conditions produces a discontinuous or thinned surface layer.
Discontinuities in the oxide layer permit oxygen ingress and internal oxidation.
Internal oxidation and barrier weakening generate localized stresses, particularly along grain boundaries.
Localized grain-boundary stresses initiate and propagate microcracks.
Microcrack propagation can ultimately cause catastrophic failure.
An oxidizing atmosphere maintains a continuous and adherent oxide scale.
A continuous oxide scale under oxidizing conditions preserves interfacial cohesion and stability.
Relative to the oxidizing baseline, reducing-gas exposure will produce more internal oxidation.
Relative to the oxidizing baseline, reducing-gas exposure will produce more grain-boundary cracking.
Relative to the oxidizing baseline, reducing-gas exposure will decrease mechanical performance, such as fracture toughness.
The proposed behavior is expected between 900 and 1100 K during cyclic thermal exposure.
The proposed behavior applies only when the gas exposure does not induce phase transformations or other microstructural changes beyond oxidation or reduction effects.
